arxiv-2203-11627.title: Centered plug-in estimation of Wasserstein distances
arxiv-2203-11627.creator: Tamás P. Papp, Chris Sherlock
arxiv-2203-11627.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Tamás P. Papp, Chris Sherlock. The plug-in estimator of the squared Euclidean 2-Wasserstein distance is conservative, however due to its large positive bias it is often uninformative. We eliminate most of this bias using a simple centering procedure based on linear combinations. We construct a pair of centered plug-in estimators that decrease with the true Wasserstein distance, and are therefore guaranteed to be informative, for any finite sample size.

arxiv-2209-12321.title: Relativistic corrections to paired production of charmonium and bottomonium in decays of the Higgs boson
arxiv-2209-12321.creator: R. N. Faustov, A. P. Martynenko, F. A. Martynenko
arxiv-2209-12321.description: Abstract Rare decay process of the Higgs boson into a pair of J / Ψ J/\Psi and Υ \Upsilon particles is studied within perturbative Standard Model and relativistic quark model. The relativistic corrections connected with the relative motion of quarks are calculated in the production amplitude and the wave functions of the bound states.

arxiv-2304-04098.title: Overview of processing techniques for surface electromyography signals
arxiv-2304-04098.creator: Manjarres-Triana Alejandra, Acevedo-Serna Juan, Ramírez-Duque Andrés A, Jiménez Mario F, Pulido-Herrera Edith, Villarejo Mayor John J
arxiv-2304-04098.description: Abstract Surface electromyography (sEMG) is a technology to assess muscle activation, which is an important component in applications related to diagnosis, treatment, progression assessment, and rehabilitation of specific individuals’ conditions. Recently, sEMG potential has been shown, since it can be used in a non-invasive manner; nevertheless, it requires careful signal analysis to support health professionals reliably.

arxiv-2312-14652.title: Cauchy numbers in type B B
arxiv-2312-14652.description: Abstract In this paper, we will introduce the Cauchy numbers of both kinds in type B and produce their corresponding exponential generating functions. Then we will provide some identities involving Cauchy, Lah, and Stirling numbers in type B through combinatorial methods.

arxiv-2512-01555.title: Augmentation and Bulk Edge Correspondence for one dimensional aperiodic tight binding operators
arxiv-2512-01555.creator: Johannes Kellendonk, Lorenzo Scaglione
arxiv-2512-01555.description: Abstract . We consider a particular class of 1D aperiodic models with the aim to understand how their internal degrees of freedom contribute to their topological invariants and the possible relations (correspondences) among them. In order to handle models with finite local complexity we introduce the principle of augmentation.

arxiv-2512-17387.title: CIFE: Code Instruction-Following Evaluation
arxiv-2512-17387.creator: Sravani Gunnu, Shanmukha Guttula, Hima Patel
arxiv-2512-17387.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to real-world code generation, where functional correctness alone is insufficient for reliable deployment, developers also expect adherence to explicit requirements for robustness , formatting , and security . Existing benchmarks primarily assess correctness through test-case execution, offering limited insight into how reliably models follow such constraints.

britannica-1911-moorcroft-william.title: Moorcroft, William (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-moorcroft-william.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-moorcroft-william.description: Article 'Moorcroft, William' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 18), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. was born in Lancashire, about 1770. He was educated as a surgeon in Liverpool; but on completing his course he resolved to devote himself to veterinary surgery, and, after studying the subject in France, began practice in London. In 1795 he published a pamphlet of directions for the medical treatment of horses, with special reference to India, and in 1800 a Cursory Account of the Methods of Shoeing Horses.

pmc-12648080.creator: Aleksandra Pękowska
pmc-12648080.description: Can individual cells retain a memory of past gene expression levels even after the stimulus has faded? In this issue of Cell Genomics, Domitilla Del Vecchio and colleagues describe an analog epigenetic memory system in which DNA methylation acts as a signal that locks in gene expression levels over time and cell divisions.

pmc-12932754.title: Multilocus sequence typing and genomic characterization of the novel Streptomyces strain SCPE-10, that resists 2,4-D toxicity and has bioremediation potential
pmc-12932754.creator: Nildo Alfredo Nhampossa, João Victor Castro de Almeida Araújo, Vicente Almeida Serafim da Silva, João Ricardo Vidal Amaral, Cinara Souza da Conceição, Carlos Alberto Xavier Gonçalves, Eamim Daidrê Squizani, Sheila da Silva, Marcia Soares Vidal, Yinglong Chen, Andrew Macrae, Rodrigo Pires do Nascimen
pmc-12932754.description: The widespread use of aromatic herbicides such as 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) has led to persistent environmental contamination, requiring efficient and sustainable biodegradation strategies. In this study, we isolated and characterized a novel actinobacterial strain, Streptomyces sp. SCPE-10, from contaminated coastal soil, capable of using 2,4-D as its sole carbon source.

pmc-13068737.title: Plasma neurofilament light chain and glial fibrillary acidic protein in the differential diagnosis of acute vertigo in the emergency department
pmc-13068737.creator: Melanie Haidegger, Natalie Berger, Simon Fandler-Höfler, Lukas Gattermeyer-Kell, Isra Hatab, Markus Kneihsl, Sebastian Monsberger, Tobias Niedrist, Cansu Tafrali, Maria Martinez-Serrat, Pascal Benkert, Jens Kuhle, Christian Enzinger, Michael Khalil, Thomas Gattringer
pmc-13068737.description: BackgroundDistinguishing posterior circulation stroke (PCS) from peripheral or other causes of acute vertigo can be challenging. Blood biomarkers, such as plasma neurofilament light chain (pNfL) and glial acidic fibrillary protein (pGFAP), have been associated with (even small) stroke lesions and could support patient selection for neuroimaging and inpatient evaluation in acute vertigo.

pmc-13077391.title: Equivalence of neoadjuvant and perioperative therapies in patients with stage III non-small cell lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis

pmc-13077391.description: BackgroundBoth neoadjuvant and perioperative immunotherapies have emerged as standard-of-care treatments for patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the optimal treatment strategy regarding the necessity of the adjuvant phase remains undefined due to a lack of direct head-to-head comparisons.

pmc-13421781.title: Vibrotactile beat sensitivity in deaf individuals: behavioral and neural evidence
pmc-13421781.creator: Sean A Gilmore, Phuong-Nghi Pham, Frank A Russo
pmc-13421781.description: Beat sensitivity is typically studied in the auditory modality, yet the temporal prediction mechanisms that support beat processing are thought to be supramodal and may be accessible through other sensory channels. Deafness provides a powerful model for examining whether these mechanisms can be recruited through somatosensory input.

pmc-13623420.title: Beyond diagnostic accuracy: evaluating the clinical utility of artificial intelligence for suspicious lesion triage
pmc-13623420.creator: Nethmi Chandrasekara
pmc-13623420.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The recent systematic review and meta-analysis by Nirula et al. reports pooled sensitivity and specificity of 89% and 82%, respectively, for artificial intelligence (AI)-based differentiation between benign and malignant skin lesions. This highlights the diagnostic potential of these tools. However, diagnostic accuracy alone does not establish clinical utility; a tool that performs well in retrospective validation may not meaningfully alter referral patterns, reduce waiting times or improve healthcare efficiency in practice.
